subject: Physics
title: Grade 9 Olympiad Kinematics Conceptual Ontology & Dependency Graph

structural_pillars.name: Galilean Superposition & Orthogonal Decoupling
structural_pillars.statement: Motion along mutually perpendicular Cartesian axes is completely independent. The position, velocity, and acceleration along the x-axis decouple from those along the y-axis, linked solely by the single shared parameter of time t.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: \vec{r}(t) = x(t)\hat{i} + y(t)\hat{j}, \quad a_x = \frac{d^2x}{dt^2}, \quad a_y = \frac{d^2y}{dt^2}, \quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial y} = 0
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Holds in all Newtonian inertial reference frames where spatial coordinate axes are orthogonal and non-rotating.

structural_pillars.name: Differential Rate Duality & Motion Graph Geometry
structural_pillars.statement: Velocity is the instantaneous time rate of change of position; acceleration is the instantaneous time rate of change of the velocity vector. Tangent slopes on coordinate-time curves represent rates; definite integrals (enclosed area) represent cumulative changes.
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Valid for all continuous kinematic trajectories, regardless of whether acceleration is constant or variable.

structural_pillars.name: Galileo's Odd-Number Invariant of Uniform Acceleration
structural_pillars.statement: For any body starting from rest under constant acceleration, the distances traversed in successive equal time intervals follow the exact ratio of consecutive odd integers: 1 : 3 : 5 : 7 : ... : (2n-1).
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: \Delta s_n = s(n\,\Delta t) - s((n-1)\,\Delta t) = \frac{1}{2}a(\Delta t)^2 (2n - 1) \implies \frac{\Delta s_n}{\Delta s_1} = 2n - 1
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Requires zero initial velocity (u = 0) and strictly constant acceleration (a = const) across all intervals.

structural_pillars.name: Parabolic Trajectory Symmetry & Height Splitting
structural_pillars.statement: Under uniform gravity with zero air resistance, horizontal velocity is invariant, making the trajectory a symmetric parabola y(x) = x tan(theta)(1 - x/R). Any intermediate height h < H is reached at two distinct times t1 and t2 symmetrically placed about apex.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: t_1 + t_2 = T = \frac{2u\sin\theta}{g}, \quad t_1 t_2 = \frac{2h}{g}, \quad h = \frac{1}{2}g t_1 t_2, \quad R = \frac{u^2\sin 2\theta}{g}
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Applies to flat-ground projectile launch in a uniform gravitational field without aerodynamic drag.

structural_pillars.name: Galilean Relative Frame Invariance & Zero Relative Acceleration
structural_pillars.statement: The relative motion between two particles is governed by vector difference r_rel = r1 - r2 and v_rel = v1 - v2. When both particles are free falling under uniform gravity, their relative acceleration is identically zero, rendering their relative trajectory a straight line.
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Requires both bodies to move under the same uniform gravitational field without additional non-gravitational external forces.

nodes.description: Declared spatial origin and clock setting the zero coordinates (x0, y0, t0).
Position vector r(t) vs cumulative scalar path length s = int |v| dt.
Net change in position vector: Delta r = r(t2) - r(t1).

nodes.term: Free Fall & Galileo's Odd Number Law

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: When a projectile or thrown ball reaches its highest point (apex), its velocity is zero, so its acceleration must also be zero.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Velocity is zero momentarily at the turnaround instant, but acceleration is the derivative dv/dt = -g != 0. If acceleration were zero at the apex, the ball would remain suspended in mid-air indefinitely.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: High-speed strobe photography and accelerometer attached to a vertical toss reveal constant -9.8 m/s^2 readout continuously through the apex.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Total distance traveled is always equal to the magnitude of displacement.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Displacement is the net vector change in position Delta r. Distance is the path integral of speed. In any round-trip or reverse motion, distance > 0 while displacement = 0.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: A runner on a 400 m circular track completes one full lap: odometer reads 400 m, but vector displacement from start to finish is exactly 0 m.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: A car travelling half the distance at v1 and the remaining half at v2 has average speed (v1 + v2) / 2.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Average speed is total distance divided by total time. For equal distances, the car spends more time at the slower speed, yielding the harmonic mean v_avg = 2*v1*v2 / (v1 + v2). The arithmetic average applies only to equal time intervals.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Driving 60 km at 30 km/h (takes 2 hours) and 60 km at 60 km/h (takes 1 hour). Total distance = 120 km, total time = 3 hours => average speed = 40 km/h, not 45 km/h.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: A bullet fired horizontally at 500 m/s will take longer to hit the ground than a bullet dropped simultaneously from the same height.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Horizontal and vertical motions decouple completely. Both bullets experience identical vertical acceleration a_y = -g with identical initial vertical velocity u_y = 0, hitting the ground simultaneously at t = sqrt(2h/g).
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Classic physics apparatus: a spring-loaded launcher simultaneously shoots one ball horizontally while dropping a second ball vertically from the same height; audio sensors record a single simultaneous ground impact click.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.concept: Motion Graph Slope vs Height Conflation
cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: On a position-time graph, when the curve crosses the time axis (x = 0), the velocity is zero; or on a velocity-time graph, a negative velocity indicates deceleration.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: On an x-t graph, velocity is the tangent slope dx/dt, not position x(t). On a v-t graph, sign indicates direction of motion; deceleration occurs if and only if velocity and acceleration have opposite signs (|v| is decreasing).
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: A car passing through x = 0 at 100 km/h has zero position but high speed. A ball tossed upward has v < 0 and a < 0 on the downward leg, meaning it is accelerating downward (speeding up).

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: If an object moves in a circle at constant speed, its acceleration is zero because speed is not changing.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Acceleration is the derivative of the velocity vector. Because the direction of velocity continuously changes, uniform circular motion requires a continuous inward centripetal acceleration a_c = v^2/r.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Whirling a stone on a string: cutting the string releases the stone tangentially in a straight line, proving the string's inward pull was continuously accelerating the stone toward the center.
